# Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold
Source: https://llms-explorer.com/tree/burstable-m10-m20-cpu-credits-and-the-m30-production-threshold/

# Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] A CPU-credit monitoring feature request contains a February 2023 report of exhausted-credit performance loss and a July 2025 report of sharply increasing M20 CPU steal. These customer accounts support investigating credit visibility, but do not independently prove that every present-day Atlas configuration lacks credit metrics. (low confidence) — https://feedback.mongodb.com/ideas/CUSTOMER-I-9170

## How it works

- [statement] CPU credits accumulate when usage stays below the instance baseline and are consumed above it. A short performance test with accumulated credits can therefore overstate sustainable capacity; test sustained load before treating M10/M20 as a cost-saving substitute for M30. The test recommendation is an inference from the mechanism and the reported load-test experience. (medium confidence) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/burstable-credits-baseline-concepts.html · keywords: Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/dip-in-opcounters-every-15-mins/194315
- [statement] A 2022 load-test participant corrected an initial M30 attribution: most testing had run on M10/M20 with high CPU steal. The participant reported smoother process CPU and application response times after using M30 for long tests, while periodic system CPU spikes remained. This is one workload report, not a universal benchmark. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/dip-in-opcounters-every-15-mins/194315
- [statement] For sustained workloads, budget for the possibility that M30 becomes the practical compute floor even when M10/M20 meet storage requirements. This is a workload-dependent cost inference from the burst cap and MongoDB’s production-sizing recommendation; it is not a claim that all production applications must upgrade. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-clusters.md · keywords: Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Atlas Core computes relative CPU utilization for M10/M20 by dividing normalized system CPU by the provider-guaranteed baseline, typically 20–50%. The baseline is not visible in Atlas metrics. With a 20% baseline, 15% normalized CPU corresponds to 75% relative CPU, so apparently low normalized utilization can still drive scaling. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Capacity planning should account for sustained CPU demand and spikes before relying on reactive scaling: MongoDB warns that resource preparation takes time and automatic scaling may not respond in time to a sudden bulk insert. Combined with the sustained-load warning for M10/M20, this supports budgeting for M30+ when a workload needs sustained production capacity. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md · keywords: Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Atlas Core autoscaling evaluates M10/M20 CPU relative to the provider's baseline rather than assuming the full nominal CPU is continuously available. Its documentation describes baseline CPU as typically 20%-50% and not visible in Atlas metrics, so 20% is an illustrative lower-bound estimate rather than a universal tier specification. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas M10 and M20 use burstable infrastructure; cloud providers cap CPU after burst periods, so sustained heavy workloads can throttle despite these tiers being dedicated clusters. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-clusters.md · keywords: Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection.md
- [statement] MongoDB recommends M30 and higher for production, but explicitly permits M10/M20 for low-traffic production applications. M30 is therefore a recommended capacity threshold, not a universal production eligibility requirement. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection.md · keywords: Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-clusters.md
- [statement] Atlas documents its System: CPU (Steal) alert for exhausted-credit AWS EC2 burstable instances, identified as M10/M20. This documented alert scope must not be generalized to every Atlas cloud provider. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/system-cpu-usage.md
- [statement] AWS distinguishes Standard from Unlimited credit modes: Standard falls back toward baseline after accrued credits run out; Unlimited can continue bursting with surplus credits and possible extra charges. This AWS capability does not establish that Atlas exposes an Unlimited-mode setting or passes such charges through. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/burstable-credits-baseline-concepts.html
- [statement] Deyan Petrov's firsthand Azure account, published in 2021 and edited in January 2025, describes M10/M20 on burstable B-series VMs and CPU-related monitoring limitations. Its instance mapping and numerical baseline are historical observations, not verified current mappings or universal Atlas guarantees. (low confidence) — https://dev.to/deyanp/mongodb-atlas-azure-a-forced-marriage-169m
- [statement] A February 2024 customer reported repeated M20-to-M30 scaling after CPU spikes associated with starting a scaled-down node. The thread poses a causal hypothesis and supplies timestamps; it does not prove a general autoscaling defect. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/cpu-measurement-after-autoscaling/265524
- [statement] For AWS burstable instances, usage below baseline adds net CPU credits and usage above baseline consumes net credits. In Standard mode, exhausting accrued credits brings CPU utilization back toward baseline. MongoDB's Atlas guidance identifies exhausted AWS M10/M20 credit balances as a condition where its CPU-steal alert applies. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/burstable-credits-baseline-concepts.html · keywords: Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/system-cpu-usage.md
- [statement] Atlas documents its CPU-steal alert for AWS EC2 burstable M10/M20 instances. An independent Azure operator also reported burstable M10/M20 behavior but missing CPU-steal monitoring; that historical report does not establish the current availability of Azure metrics. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/system-cpu-usage.md · keywords: Burstable M10/M20 CPU credits and the M30 production threshold · also: https://dev.to/deyanp/mongodb-atlas-azure-a-forced-marriage-169m
